questions.prompt: Which statement about Kingdom Fungi is FALSE?

options.text: Fungi can be unicellular or multicellular.
Fungi are motile, using flagella to move toward food sources.
The fungal cell wall is made of chitin.

why.A: True — fungi can be one-celled or many-celled.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes yeasts from molds?

options.text: Yeasts are multicellular; molds are unicellular
Yeasts are aerobic only; molds are facultative anaerobes
Yeasts are unicellular facultative anaerobes; molds are multicellular and aerobic
Yeasts reproduce only sexually; molds only asexually

questions.explanation: Yeasts are unicellular facultative anaerobes; molds are multicellular and aerobic.

why.B: Yeasts can ferment; molds are aerobic.

questions.prompt: Describe the process of budding in yeast, including what happens to the chitin cell wall when a bud breaks off.
questions.explanation: In budding, a yeast cell doesn't split in half; instead it grows a small bud off to the side, copies its chromosome into the bud, and the bud eventually breaks off to form a new, independent cell. Where the bud breaks off, it leaves a "bud scar" in the chitin cell wall.

questions.prompt: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is important because it:

options.text: Ferments sugar into CO2 and ethanol, used in bread and alcohol production

questions.explanation: Ferments sugar into CO2 and ethanol, used in bread and alcohol production.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a hypha and the mycelium?
questions.explanation: A hypha is a single filament of fungal cells; the mycelium is the entire network of many hyphae that make up a mold.

questions.prompt: Which statement about sporangiospores and conidiospores is FALSE?

options.text: Sporangiospores are enclosed on a sporangiophore.
Conidiospores are exposed on a conidiophore.
Both are types of asexual spores.
These spore types are both associated with molds.

questions.explanation: False. Aspergillus and Penicillium produce conidiospores, not sporangiospores.

options.text: Sexual reproduction, with hyphae of opposite mating types fusing underground
Binary fission of a single yeast cell

questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction, with hyphae of opposite mating types fusing underground.

why.A: Mushrooms come from sexual fusion, not budding.
why.C: Binary fission is for single cells.

questions.prompt: Why are antifungal drugs difficult to develop, compared to antibacterial drugs?
questions.explanation: Human and fungal cells are both eukaryotic and biochemically/metabolically very similar, so there are few exploitable differences to target with a drug - unlike bacteria, which offer clear targets like peptidoglycan or the prokaryotic (70S) ribosome.

questions.prompt: Which molecule do fungal cell membranes use to regulate fluidity, in place of the cholesterol used by human cells?
Compare how miconazole (Monistat) and anidulafungin (Eraxis) each work, including which fungal structure each targets.
questions.explanation: Miconazole (Monistat) inhibits ergosterol synthesis, disrupting the fungal cell membrane. Anidulafungin (Eraxis) instead inhibits cell wall (chitin) synthesis - a different fungal structure entirely.

why.C: A mycosis is a disease, not a drug.

questions.prompt: How did Alexander Fleming discover penicillin?
questions.explanation: Fleming had a plate of growing bacteria that became contaminated with a Penicillium mold colony. He noticed bacterial cells near the mold were dying while cells farther away survived, suggesting the mold was releasing a substance that killed the bacteria which turned out to be penicillin.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a mold that produces conidiospores?

options.text: None of the above; all yeasts produce conidiospores

why.D: Yeasts bud; conidiospores come from molds.

questions.prompt: Which statement about chitin is FALSE?

options.text: It makes up the fungal cell wall.
It is also found in arthropod exoskeletons.
It is chemically similar to cellulose.
It is the sterol that regulates fungal membrane fluidity.
It is a polymer of glucosamine.

questions.explanation: False. Chitin is the cell wall material, not a sterol; ergosterol is the sterol that regulates fungal membrane fluidity.

why.A: True — chitin is the fungal wall.
